name: Mountain pose
why: Tall, balanced standing: the starting point of standing flows and a calm place to settle your breath.
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, weight even across both feet.
Arms by your sides, palms facing forward.
cues: Grow tall through the crown of your head
feel: Lightly working legs and a tall, easy spine.
stopIf: You feel dizzy or light-headed: sit down.

media.credit: Video: Mountain Pose (Tadasana) - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Standing forward fold
why: Lengthens the backs of the legs and lets the spine hang and relax.
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward from your hips and let your upper body hang.
cues: Bend your knees as much as you need
mistakes: Locking the knees and rounding hard
Forcing your hands to the floor
feel: A stretch along the back of the legs and a gentle release in the back.
stopIf: Back pain, or pain or tingling down a leg. Come up slowly to avoid dizziness.
cautions: Head below the heart: keep it brief or skip it if you have uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma or a detached retina.

media.credit: Video: Forward Fold Yoga Pose - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Half forward fold
why: A flat-back hinge that links poses in a sun salutation and teaches hip hinging.
setup: From a forward fold, put your hands on your shins or thighs.
feel: Back of the legs lengthening, back muscles gently working.
stopIf: Back pain.

media.credit: Video: Half Standing Forward Bend (Ardha Uttanasana) - Yoga Pose Tutorial by Muscle and Motion (Muscle & Motion)

name: Downward-facing dog
why: Stretches the calves and hamstrings while the arms and shoulders carry weight: a classic whole-body pose.
setup: From hands and knees, tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back.
cues: Push the floor away with your hands
Lift your hips up and back
Bend your knees to keep your back long
mistakes: Rounding the back to get the heels down
Hands too close to the feet
feel: Stretch in calves and backs of the legs, work in the arms and shoulders.
stopIf: Wrist or shoulder pain, or you feel dizzy.
cautions: Head below the heart: keep it brief or skip it if you have uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma or a detached retina.
Wrist pain: try it on your forearms (dolphin) or skip it.

media.credit: Video: Downward Dog - Downward Facing Dog Yoga Pose (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Low lunge
why: Opens the front of the hip and thigh, which tighten with sitting and running.
setup: Kneel on padding, then step one foot forward into a lunge.
Hands on the front knee or reaching up.
cues: Lift your chest, arms up if steady
feel: A stretch at the front of the back leg's hip and thigh.
stopIf: Pain in either knee, or in the lower back.

media.credit: Video: Low Lunge Pose (Anjaneyasana) - Parker University Yoga (Parker University)

name: Warrior II
why: A strong standing pose that builds leg strength and opens the hips and inner thighs.
setup: Step your feet wide apart, front toes forward, back toes turned in slightly.
Bend the front knee, arms out at shoulder height.
feel: Work in the front thigh, a stretch in the inner thighs.
stopIf: Knee pain above about 3 out of 10.

media.credit: Video: Warrior 2 Yoga Pose - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Triangle pose
why: Stretches the sides of the body, hamstrings and inner thighs while building balance.
setup: Stand with feet wide, front toes forward.
Reach forward over the front leg, then tip down: hand on shin, a block or a chair.
cues: Both legs straight, front knee soft
Reach forward, then tip your arm down
Open your chest to the side
mistakes: Collapsing the side of the waist
Forcing the hand to the floor
feel: A stretch along the front-leg hamstring and the side of the body.
stopIf: Back or knee pain.

media.credit: Video: Triangle Pose  |  Trikonasana  |  Foundations of Yoga (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Tree pose
why: A balance pose that trains the ankle, foot and hip muscles to keep you steady.
setup: Stand on one leg near a wall if needed.
Place the other foot on the inside of the ankle, calf or thigh.
cues: Foot on ankle, calf or thigh, never the knee
Fix your gaze on one spot
mistakes: Foot pressing on the knee joint
Hip pushing out to the side
feel: Small muscles in the standing foot and ankle working, hips steady.
stopIf: Ankle or knee pain.

media.credit: Video: Tree Pose - Vrksasana - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Chair pose
why: A held half-squat that builds strength in the legs and buttocks.
setup: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and sit back, arms up or hands at the chest.
cues: Sit back as if into a chair
feel: Hard work in the thighs and buttocks.
stopIf: Knee pain above about 3 out of 10.

media.credit: Video: Chair Pose | Utkatasana (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Plank
why: Builds trunk and shoulder strength; the link between poses in a sun salutation.
setup: From hands and knees, step your feet back into a straight line.
Hands under the shoulders.
cues: Knees down to make it easier
feel: Work in the stomach, shoulders and arms.
stopIf: Wrist, shoulder or back pain.

media.credit: Video: Plank Pose - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Low cobra
why: A gentle backbend that strengthens the back muscles and opens the chest.
setup: Lie face down, hands beside your chest, elbows tucked in.
Legs long, tops of the feet down.
cues: Lift your chest with your back muscles
mistakes: Pushing up high on straight arms
feel: Work along the back and a stretch across the front of the chest.
stopIf: Back pain increases, or pain spreads into a leg.

media.credit: Video: How to Do Cobra Pose Safely | Beginner Yoga Guide (MyYogaTeacher)

name: Sphinx pose
why: The gentlest backbend, propped on the forearms. Many backs that feel better standing up straight like it.
setup: Lie face down and prop yourself up on your forearms, elbows under your shoulders.
cues: Let your belly soften to the floor
mistakes: Pushing up higher than is comfortable
feel: A gentle arch in the lower back, easing with each breath.
stopIf: Back pain increases, or pain spreads into a leg (some backs prefer bending forward).

media.credit: Video: How to Do Sphinx Pose | Gentle Heart Opening Yoga for Posture and Back Strength (Lauren McMillin | Yoga & Movement)

name: Bridge pose (held)
why: Strengthens the buttocks and backs of the legs while opening the front of the hips.
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet hip-width apart near your bottom.
cues: Press your feet down and lift your hips
Lower slowly, one vertebra at a time
feel: Glutes and backs of the thighs working.
stopIf: Back or neck pain.

media.credit: Video: Bridge Pose - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Seated forward fold
why: A quiet, calming stretch for the backs of the legs and the back.
setup: Sit on a folded blanket or cushion with your legs out in front.
Bend your knees as much as you need.
cues: Sit tall on a cushion, knees bent if needed
mistakes: Rounding hard to reach the toes
feel: A stretch along the backs of the legs.
stopIf: Tingling down the legs, or back pain.

media.credit: Video: Seated Forward Fold Yoga Tutorial | Personalize Your Practice with Props (Mindful Yoga with Dr. Beth)

name: Butterfly pose
why: Opens the inner thighs and hips. Gentle enough to hold for a while.
setup: Sit on a cushion with the soles of your feet together, knees out to the sides.
feel: A stretch along the inner thighs.
stopIf: Groin or knee pain.

media.credit: Video: Bound Angle  Pose - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Lying twist
why: A relaxing twist for the back, good at the end of the day.
setup: Lie on your back, arms out in a T.
Draw one knee up and let it fall across your body.
cues: Draw one knee across your body
Look the other way if comfortable
mistakes: Forcing the knee to the floor
feel: Gentle rotation and stretch through the back and outer hip.
stopIf: Back pain or pain into a leg.

media.credit: Video: Reclined Twist Yoga Pose - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Happy baby
why: Releases the hips and lower back in a supported, relaxed position.
setup: Lie on your back, hug your knees in, then hold the outsides of your feet or your shins.
cues: Lower back relaxed on the floor
mistakes: Lifting the head and straining the neck
feel: A stretch in the inner thighs and hips.
stopIf: Hip pinching or knee pain.

media.credit: Video: Happy Baby | Yoga Poses | YogaRenew How To Yoga Pose Video (YogaRenew)

name: Lying hamstring stretch with a strap
why: A back-friendly hamstring stretch: the floor supports your spine.
setup: Lie on your back with a strap, belt or towel round one foot.
The other leg long on the floor, or bent.
cues: Strap or towel round one foot
Raise the leg to a gentle stretch
feel: A stretch in the back of the raised leg.
stopIf: Tingling or pain down the leg: ease off.

media.credit: Video: Hamstring Stretch with a Strap, Supine - Ask Doctor Jo (AskDoctorJo)

name: Legs up the wall
why: A restful pose that eases tired legs after running or hiking and helps you wind down.
setup: Sit side-on to a wall, then swing your legs up as you lie back.
Bottom close to the wall, legs resting on it.
mistakes: Straining to get the bottom right against the wall
feel: Legs relaxing, a gentle stretch in the backs of the legs.
stopIf: Tingling or numbness in the legs: bend the knees or come down.
cautions: Skip it in late pregnancy, or if you have glaucoma or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

media.credit: Video: How to do Viparita Karani (Legs Up the Wall) w/ AnaMargret Sanchez (Yoga International)

name: Relaxation (savasana)
why: A few minutes of complete rest at the end of a session lets your body and mind settle.
setup: Lie on your back, arms and legs relaxed, palms up. A cushion under the knees helps the back.
cues: Let your whole body get heavy
feel: Calm, heavy and relaxed.
stopIf: You feel unwell: roll to your side and sit up slowly.

media.credit: Video: Corpse Pose - Yoga With Adriene (Yoga With Adriene)

name: Belly breathing
why: Slow breathing with a long breath out calms the nervous system, which can ease stress and the way pain is felt.
setup: Sit or lie comfortably.
One hand on your belly, one on your chest.
cues: Breathe in through your nose, belly rises
feel: Calm; the belly hand moves more than the chest hand.
stopIf: You feel dizzy or light-headed: breathe normally.

media.credit: Video: Deep Belly Breathing (Diaphragmatic Breathing) for Stress Relief (National Cancer Centre Singapore)

name: Box breathing
why: Breathing in a steady 4-4-4-4 rhythm is a simple way to settle nerves before sport or after a stressful day.
setup: Sit tall and relax your shoulders.
feel: Calm and steady.
stopIf: You feel dizzy: shorten the holds or breathe normally.

media.credit: Video: Box Breathing Technique and Exercise | 1 Minute | Use For Meditation, Anxiety, Or Sleep | 4 4 4 4 (Sandstone Care)
